five_whys_trace.q: Why does mcphost need `.gitattributes` merge=union entries for CHANGELOG.md, www/llms.txt, and .buildloop/extended-gates.toml?
five_whys_trace.a: Two build-loop incidents on 2026-09-17 (gate-debt-4f1112d land exit 10 on agent/intent-card.json, and agent-consent land-conflict 01:45Z on 11 files, 4 of them generated or append-only) showed rebase conflicts landing on files nobody meant to treat as ordinary source (PRD grounding).

five_whys_trace.q: Why did those files conflict textually instead of resolving automatically?
five_whys_trace.a: git's default merge driver treats every tracked file as ordinary text; nothing in mcphost declared CHANGELOG.md/www/llms.txt/.buildloop/extended-gates.toml as append-only.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is that still a problem once the build loop has its own fix?
five_whys_trace.a: land-resolve.sh (this PRD's R2/R3, landed in build-skill) now union-merges these three files automatically inside the loop, but an operator running a manual git rebase/merge on this repo outside the loop gets none of that -- the exact textual conflict the loop just learned to avoid.

five_whys_trace.q: Why fix it via .gitattributes here rather than only the loop-side policy file?
five_whys_trace.a: merge=union is git's own mechanism for exactly this case, and this PRD's R6 asks for it explicitly "so an operator's manual rebase behaves the same way" -- the two mechanisms (state/land-policy/mcphost.json for the loop, .gitattributes for git itself) name the same three paths so they cannot silently diverge.

five_whys_trace.q: Why land it as its own small commit through the normal mcphost PR path rather than bundled with build-skill's changes?
five_whys_trace.a: build-skill and mcphost are different repos with different gates; R6 states this file is "committed through the normal mcphost landing path (a loop/ PR), cited in receipts" -- a single-purpose, reviewable commit keeps this branch's gate diff scoped to exactly these three attribute lines.
